name: India–Pakistan
value: Indus treaty in abeyance; no LoC strike found
summary: Pakistan called India's Indus Waters Treaty suspension 'outlaw behaviour' at the UN on 18–19 Nov; no LoC exchange found
state: At UN Security Council meetings on 18–19 Nov, Pakistan said India's holding of the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance amounted to weaponising water, and India's envoy said the world had changed since the treaty was signed (Dawn, 19 Nov). Indian troops fired at suspected movement near the Line of Control in Poonch's Sajwan sector early on 16 Nov; no casualties or exchange with Pakistani forces were reported (WION). No cross-border strike or mobilisation was found as of 20 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No change for most travellers, but areas near the Line of Control remain sensitive. Check FCDO travel advice for India and Pakistan, which advises against travel to parts of Kashmir.
rubric_hit: Watch: treaty suspension (Indus Waters Treaty held in abeyance) and LoC firing at suspected infiltration (16 Nov); no cross-border strike

sources.title: Dawn — India's move on Indus Waters Treaty is 'outlaw behaviour', Pakistan tells UN
WION — Army opens fire after suspected movement near LoC in Poonch's Sajwan sector

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
